questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify and comment on any three pillars of Islam that demonstrate unity and solidarity as an expression of Islam.

(20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The five pillars of Islam (the declaration of faith *shahada*, prayer *salah*, almsgiving *zakat*, fasting *sawm* and pilgrimage *hajj*) are acts of worship, but they also bind Muslims into one community. Three that show unity and solidarity especially clearly are prayer, almsgiving and pilgrimage.

**1. Prayer (salah).**
(i) All Muslims, everywhere in the world, face the same direction, towards the Ka'ba in Makkah, and use the same Arabic words and movements.
(ii) In congregational prayer, worshippers stand shoulder to shoulder in straight rows, without distinction of rank, wealth or race; the poor may stand next to the rich and the ruler next to the labourer.
(iii) The Friday prayer and the prayers of the two feasts bring the community together, and the sermon addresses its shared concerns.
(iv) Prayer therefore expresses equality before God and the unity of the believers.

**2. Almsgiving (zakat).**
(i) Muslims who own more than a minimum amount of wealth must give a fixed portion, commonly 2.5 per cent of their savings, each year to people in need.
(ii) The Qur'an names the categories of beneficiaries, including the poor, the needy and those in debt.
(iii) Zakat reduces the gap between rich and poor, removes envy, and makes the wealthy responsible for the welfare of others.
(iv) It also promotes solidarity because the community cares for its weakest members.

**3. Pilgrimage (hajj).**
(i) Millions of Muslims from every country, language and class gather in Makkah at the same time.
(ii) All men wear the same simple white garments (*ihram*), which removes signs of status.
(iii) They perform the same rites together and call on God with the same words.
(iv) The pilgrimage shows the unity of the world Muslim community (the *ummah*) and strengthens ties between believers.

**4. Other pillars briefly.** Fasting in Ramadan is also shared: all Muslims fast at the same time, which makes the rich feel the hunger of the poor, and ends with the feast of Id-ul-Fitr and the gift of food to the needy.

**Conclusion.** Prayer, zakat and the Hajj are personal duties to God, but through them Islam builds a community in which believers stand equal before God and care for one another.
